quote: No. This is Debbie. It's wife.
stewart_read: Debbie self-identifies as Mike's wife in the first exchange — an immediate co-owner/spouse signal. The rep says 'Oh, okay' and moves straight into his pitch to her without asking if Mike is available, on title, or should be looped in.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply adapted to whoever picked up, standard practice on a cold dial. Strategic read is not supported — there's no later attempt to loop Mike back in or confirm Debbie's ownership status, so this reads as a missed protocol trigger rather than a deliberate choice to proceed with Debbie.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pause on a wrong-person pickup: confirm whether the person on the line is a co-owner, and if not the named lead, ask directly whether they're on title or if the actual lead should be present before running the full pitch.

quote: Yeah. And then you know about the bill swap too?
stewart_read: Before any qualification (no bill captured, no interest reason established, ownership unclear), the rep volunteers Ion's financial mechanism — closer-tier content. This is the exact anti-pattern the schema flags: giving away appointment value prematurely instead of using the universal escape hatch to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep may have been trying to re-hook a skeptical customer with a concrete value prop. Rejected — the explanation is detailed (mechanism, savings guarantee, no upfront cost) and delivered without first re-establishing any qualification, which is scope creep regardless of intent.
coaching_implication: Redirect the rep to the escape hatch language: qualify first, then bridge financial mechanism questions to the specialist rather than explaining the full program mechanics himself.

quote: Oh, I see. Okay. Well, that's good to know. I can direct I can direct people to that if they ask about it
stewart_read: Debbie explicitly says she'd use this information to direct OTHER people, not herself — a direct statement that she isn't the prospect. The rep does not re-qualify at this moment (doesn't ask who actually wants solar, doesn't re-anchor on her own home's interest), letting the call continue as if she were a live lead.
coaching_implication: When a customer says they're gathering info for others, that is the moment to stop and re-run the interest/homeowner qualifier explicitly — confirm whose name should actually be on the appointment.

quote: Okay. So the the concern there. Yeah. I mean, we can I can help you build the design or even just, like, kinda price you out, and then you can talk to a specialist to see what we can do for you?
stewart_read: Rep again blurs the setter/closer line, offering to personally 'build the design' or 'price her out' rather than cleanly routing to the specialist. Combined with the 01:14 bill-swap explanation, this is a second instance of the same scope pattern in one short call.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read supported: rep appears to be improvising to keep the customer engaged after she's twice deflected, not executing a deliberate strategy.
coaching_implication: Reinforce the single clean bridge line ('that's exactly what the specialist walks you through') rather than layering in more self-offered detail when a customer hesitates.

stewart_read: Debbie's question about company location is really a trust/legitimacy probe, and the rep's answer ('The company's everywhere. I'm just at the Utah's, like, location') is vague and doesn't reinforce legitimacy the way the intro's Tesla/certified framing is designed to.
coaching_implication: Coach a tighter, more specific answer to location/legitimacy questions — specificity reduces suspicion per the protocol; vagueness here does the opposite.

quote: Please just send my husband email, and and we'll go from there.
stewart_read: The customer offers a clear next-step request — email her husband, the actual named lead — and the rep does not capture the email address or Mike's contact info at all, instead offering to text Debbie's own number.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep may have judged a text to Debbie was more likely to get a response than chasing an email for Mike. Not well supported — the rep never asks for the email or confirms Mike's contact details, so this reads as a missed capture rather than a deliberate channel choice.
coaching_implication: When the customer directs the rep to a specific next step (email the husband), the rep should capture that concretely — get the email address — rather than substituting his own preferred channel unprompted.

quote: I can hear. I can just text you, and you can always have my number. And if you want Okay. Text me back, you can.
stewart_read: No day, no time, no appointment mechanics — the call ends on a vague mutual-text arrangement with no owned next step. This doesn't map cleanly to button_up (there was never an appointment being booked to button up); it's simply an ending with no procedural anchor at all.
coaching_implication: Even when a call is trending toward no-appointment, the rep should still try to lock a concrete next contact point (specific day/time to follow up, or the husband's direct number) rather than a generic 'text me back' offer.
